# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Busso_2017_exerciseTraining"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Busso_2017_exerciseTraining"))$description`
* Article: [Sci Rep 2017;7:40422](https://doi.org/10.1038/srep40422) (open access, CC BY 4.0)
* Supplementary Information (raw data, Supplementary Table S1) and Supplementary Spreadsheet (an implementation of Models T and TI): <https://www.nature.com/articles/srep40422#Sec14>

Busso (2017) carries the indirect-response idea from pharmacodynamics over to
exercise training. The "dose" is the daily amount of training `W` in
arbitrary training units (tu), computed from the number of 5-min repetitions
and their intensity (Methods, Equation 17), with 100 tu counted for each
performance test. Each day's training adds to a **secondary signal**, which
dissipates first-order (`kout_s`) and is transformed into **production of
performance** (`kon_s`). Performance is lost first-order (`koff`) and returns
to its baseline when training stops. In Model TI, the paper's preferred
model, production is also **inhibited** in proportion to the same day's
training (`Inhib = kin_i * W`), so a hard session lowers the benefit of the
signal accumulated from earlier sessions.

The paper compares four models: T (signal only), TI (signal plus inhibition),
TF (signal plus a fatigue term) and TIF (both). It retains Model TI because
the fatigue term came out with the wrong sign in five of the six subjects
(Results). Only Model TI has published parameter estimates (Table 2), so
only Model TI is packaged. Model T is Model TI with `kin_i = 0`, and the
authors' spreadsheet gives its fit for subject 1, which is used as an
extra check below.

# Population

Six healthy men trained on a cycle ergometer for 15 weeks: 8 weeks of three
sessions per week, one week without training, 4 weeks of five sessions per
week, and 2 weeks without training (Methods, "Experimental data"; the data
come from Busso 2003). Performance was the mean power of a 5-min maximal
test (Plim5', in W), measured 40 to 46 times per subject. Each subject was
fitted separately by maximum likelihood, so the paper reports six individual
parameter sets (Table 2) and no between-subject variance. The packaged
typical values are the medians of those six estimates, the values the paper
simulates with (Figures 5 and 6).

```{r population}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Busso_2017_exerciseTraining"))
str(ui$population)
```

# Source trace

| Element | Value in the model | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `dPerf/dt = kon - koff * Perf` (no training) | `d/dt(perf)` with `kout = koff` | Equation 1 |
| Signal production and dissipation | `signal` dosed with `W`; decay `kout_s + kon_s * (1 - Inhib)` | Equation 2 (printed with `Prec` for `Signal`), Equation 13 |
| Production `Prod = kon0 + kon_s * (1 - Inhib) * Signal` | `fprod * signal` plus `kout * rbase` | Equations 4, 11 and 14 |
| `Inhib = kin_i * W` (same-day training) | `inhib <- kinhib * w_today` | Equations 5 and 12 |
| Daily recursion `Perf(i) = Perf(i-1) exp(-koff) + Prod(i-1)` | reproduced exactly at whole days (see below) | Equation 7 |
| `kon0 = Perf0 (1 - exp(-koff))`, baseline stationary | zero-order term `kout * rbase` | Equations 8 and 9 |
| `Perf0` | 250 W (fixed) | Figure 6 caption; per subject, the first measured performance |
| `koff` | 0.03055 1/day | Table 2, median of six (Results text: 0.0305) |
| `kon_s` | 0.00739 1/day | Table 2, median of six (Results text: 0.0074) |
| `kout_s` | 0.2915 1/day | Table 2, median of six (Results text: 0.292) |
| `kin_i` | 0.00206 1/tu | Table 2, median of six (Results text: 0.0021) |
| Residual error | additive, 6.02 W | Equation 18 (Gaussian likelihood, variance profiled out); value derived below |
| Order of the inhibition term in the signal decay | day `i - 1` inhibition on the decay from day `i - 1` to day `i` | Supplementary Spreadsheet, sheet `Model_TI`, column E |

# From the paper's daily recursion to an ODE

The paper writes the model as ODEs (Equations 1 to 6) but fits and simulates
it as a once-daily recursion (Equations 7 to 14): the signal just after
day `i`'s training is `Signal(i)`, the day's production is
`Prod(i) = kon0 + kon_s (1 - Inhib(i)) Signal(i)`, and
`Perf(i + 1) = Perf(i) exp(-koff) + Prod(i)`. A plain ODE implementation of
Equations 1 to 4 does not give the same numbers, because the recursion adds
the whole day's production at once while the signal is still at its
post-training value. For the median parameters the difference is about
16% in the gain from a session, enough to miss Figures 5 and 6.

The packaged model reproduces the recursion exactly at whole days:

* each day's training `W` is a bolus into `signal` at the start of the day
  (time in days, day `i` at `time = i`);
* the inhibition for the day is read back from that dose with
  `podo(signal)` while `tad(signal) < 1`, and is zero on days without a
  training record;
* inside a day the signal decays as `exp(-kloss_signal t)`, so the production
  coefficient `fprod = kon_s (1 - Inhib) (kloss_signal - koff) / (exp(-koff) - exp(-kloss_signal))`
  makes the within-day integral deliver exactly `kon_s (1 - Inhib) Signal(i)`
  to performance by the end of the day, and the zero-order term
  `koff * Perf0` delivers exactly `kon0`.

Performance between whole days is a smooth interpolation that the paper does
not define. Give at most one training record per day, at the start of the
day. Days without training need no record.

```{r data-long}
dat <- s1 |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-day, names_to = c(".value", "id"), names_pattern = "([WP])([1-6])") |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = as.integer(id)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, day)
dat |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    days = dplyr::n(),
    training_days = sum(W > 0),
    total_tu = round(sum(W)),
    n_perf = sum(!is.na(P)),
    first_perf_W = P[!is.na(P)][1]
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Supplementary Table S1 per subject (40 to 46 performance tests, Methods).")
stopifnot(identical(
  as.integer(table(dat$id[!is.na(dat$P)])),
  c(45L, 45L, 46L, 40L, 45L, 45L)
))
```

```{r table2}
tab2 <- data.frame(
  id = 1:6,

  kon_s = c(0.00845, 0.00462, 0.00071, 0.00783, 0.00695, 0.03751),

meds <- vapply(tab2[-1], median, numeric(1))
meds

stopifnot(max(abs(th / meds - 1)) < 1e-12)
```

## Simulation helpers

```{r helpers}
mod <- readModelDb("Busso_2017_exerciseTraining")

# Event table for one subject: daily training as boluses into `signal`, and
# an observation of `perf` at every whole day so the integrator restarts at
# each day boundary.
make_events <- function(day, W) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(time = day[W > 0], amt = W[W > 0], evid = 1L, cmt = "signal"),
    data.frame(time = c(0, day), amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "perf")
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(id = 1L) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

# Solve with one subject's parameters; returns perf at the whole days `day`.
solve_subject <- function(day, W, perf0, koff, kon_s, kout_s, kin_i) {
  m <- suppressMessages(rxode2::ini(
    mod,
    lrbase = log(perf0), lkout = log(koff), lkon_signal = log(kon_s),
    lkout_signal = log(kout_s), lkinhib = log(kin_i)
  ))
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(m, make_events(day, W), returnType = "data.frame",
                         rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-10)
  out <- out[!duplicated(out$time), ]
  out$perf[match(day, out$time)]
}

# The authors' spreadsheet recursion (Supplementary Spreadsheet, sheet
# Model_TI), written out independently of the packaged model.
recursion <- function(W, perf0, koff, kon_s, kout_s, kin_i) {
  kon0 <- perf0 * (1 - exp(-koff))
  perf <- numeric(length(W))
  s_prev <- 0; inhib_prev <- 0; prod_prev <- kon0; perf_prev <- perf0
  for (i in seq_along(W)) {
    inhib <- kin_i * W[i]
    s <- W[i] + s_prev * exp(-kon_s * (1 - inhib_prev) - kout_s)
    prod <- kon0 + s * kon_s * (1 - inhib)
    perf[i] <- prod_prev + perf_prev * exp(-koff)
    s_prev <- s; inhib_prev <- inhib; prod_prev <- prod; perf_prev <- perf[i]
  }
  perf
}
```

# Check 1: the ODE reproduces the authors' recursion

Each subject is solved with their own Table 2 estimates and their own first
measured performance as `Perf0`, then compared with the spreadsheet recursion
written out in R.

```{r check-recursion}
fits <- lapply(1:6, function(j) {
  d <- dat[dat$id == j, ]
  p <- tab2[j, ]
  perf0 <- d$P[!is.na(d$P)][1]
  ode <- solve_subject(d$day, d$W, perf0, p$koff, p$kon_s, p$kout_s, p$kin_i)
  rec <- recursion(d$W, perf0, p$koff, p$kon_s, p$kout_s, p$kin_i)
  data.frame(id = j, day = d$day, W = d$W, P = d$P, ode = ode, rec = rec)
})
fits <- dplyr::bind_rows(fits)
fits |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(max_abs_diff_W = signif(max(abs(ode - rec)), 2)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Largest difference between the packaged ODE and the daily recursion over 109 days.")
# Both sides use the same parameters; the difference is integration error
# only (measured ~4e-7 W at rtol = atol = 1e-10).
stopifnot(max(abs(fits$ode - fits$rec)) < 1e-5)
```

# Check 2: goodness of fit of Model TI (Table 1)

With the residual variance profiled out of the Gaussian likelihood
(Equation 18), the negative log-likelihood is
`n/2 (log(2 pi) + 1 - log(n) + log(RSS))`, and the paper's adjusted R2 and
AICc (Equations 20 and 21, `p = 4` parameters for Model TI) follow from the
residual sum of squares.

```{r table1}
gof <- function(y, yhat, p) {
  ok <- !is.na(y)
  rss <- sum((y[ok] - yhat[ok])^2)
  tss <- sum((y[ok] - mean(y[ok]))^2)
  n <- sum(ok)
  nll <- 0.5 * n * (log(2 * pi) + 1 - log(n) + log(rss))
  c(
    n = n, rss = rss,
    adjR2 = 1 - (n - 1) / (n - p) * (rss / tss),
    AICc = 2 * p + 2 * nll + 2 * p * (p + 1) / (n - p - 1),
    sigma = sqrt(rss / n)
  )
}
tab1 <- data.frame(
  id = 1:6,
  adjR2_paper = c(0.967, 0.932, 0.920, 0.950, 0.965, 0.935),
  AICc_paper = c(291.07, 299.27, 312.77, 265.16, 281.39, 312.56)
)
gof_ti <- fits |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::reframe(as.data.frame(t(gof(P, ode, p = 4)))) |>
  dplyr::left_join(tab1, by = "id")
gof_ti |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Subject = id, n, RSS = round(rss, 1),
    "Adj. R2 (sim)" = round(adjR2, 3), "Adj. R2 (Table 1)" = adjR2_paper,
    "AICc (sim)" = round(AICc, 2), "AICc (Table 1)" = AICc_paper,
    "sigma = sqrt(RSS/n) (W)" = round(sigma, 2)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Model TI goodness of fit with the Table 2 estimates, against Table 1.")
# Table 2 prints three significant figures; refitting is not needed to land
# within the rounding of Table 1 (largest adj. R2 gap 0.002, subject 6).
stopifnot(
  max(abs(gof_ti$adjR2 - gof_ti$adjR2_paper)) < 0.005,
  max(abs(gof_ti$AICc - gof_ti$AICc_paper)) < 2
)
```

The residual error in the packaged model is the median of the six
per-subject `sigma` values:

```{r sigma}
median(gof_ti$sigma)
stopifnot(abs(median(gof_ti$sigma) - ui$theta[["addSd"]]) < 0.01)
```

## Model T for subject 1

The Model T sheet of the Supplementary Spreadsheet carries subject 1's
Model T estimates (`koff` 0.0844829, `kon_s` 0.00294108, `kout_s` 0.0815401).
Model T is the packaged model with `kin_i` set to zero.

```{r model-t}
d1 <- dat[dat$id == 1, ]
perf_t <- solve_subject(d1$day, d1$W, 253, 0.0844829085170162,
                        0.00294108281488496, 0.0815400703894475, 1e-300)
g_t <- gof(d1$P, perf_t, p = 3)
round(g_t[c("adjR2", "AICc")], 3)
# Table 1, subject 1, Model T: adj. R2 0.923, AICc 328.04
stopifnot(abs(g_t[["adjR2"]] - 0.923) < 0.001, abs(g_t[["AICc"]] - 328.04) < 0.05)
```

# Replicate Figure 3: fits of Model TI in the six subjects

```{r figure3, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(fits, aes(day)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = ode), colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(aes(y = P), data = fits[!is.na(fits$P), ], size = 1.2) +
  facet_wrap(~id, scales = "free_y", labeller = label_both) +
  labs(x = "Day", y = "Performance (W)",
       title = "Replicates Figure 3 of Busso 2017",
       caption = "Points: Supplementary Table S1. Line: packaged model with each subject's Table 2 estimates.")
```

# Replicate Figure 4: subject 1

Daily production and removal of performance are read back from the solved
performance: removal over day `i` is `Perf(i) (1 - exp(-koff))` and
production is `Perf(i + 1) - Perf(i) exp(-koff)`.

```{r figure4, fig.height = 6}
p1 <- tab2[1, ]
f1 <- fits[fits$id == 1, ]
grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 109, by = 0.05), d1$day)))
ev_fine <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(time = d1$day[d1$W > 0], amt = d1$W[d1$W > 0], evid = 1L, cmt = "signal"),
  data.frame(time = grid, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "perf")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L) |>
  dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))
m1 <- suppressMessages(rxode2::ini(
  mod, lrbase = log(253), lkout = log(p1$koff), lkon_signal = log(p1$kon_s),
  lkout_signal = log(p1$kout_s), lkinhib = log(p1$kin_i)
))
sim1 <- rxode2::rxSolve(m1, ev_fine, returnType = "data.frame")
perf_next <- c(f1$ode[-1], NA)
fig4 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(panel = "A: performance (W)", day = f1$day, value = f1$ode, what = "model"),
  data.frame(panel = "B: production / removal (W/day)", day = f1$day,
             value = perf_next - f1$ode * exp(-p1$koff), what = "production"),
  data.frame(panel = "B: production / removal (W/day)", day = f1$day,
             value = f1$ode * (1 - exp(-p1$koff)), what = "removal"),
  data.frame(panel = "C: signal (tu)", day = sim1$time, value = sim1$signal, what = "signal"),
  data.frame(panel = "D: inhibition", day = d1$day, value = p1$kin_i * d1$W, what = "inhibition")
)
ggplot(fig4, aes(day, value, colour = what)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(aes(day, P), data = data.frame(panel = "A: performance (W)", d1[!is.na(d1$P), ]),
             inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Day", y = NULL, colour = NULL, title = "Replicates Figure 4 of Busso 2017 (subject 1)")
```

Production dips below removal on each heavy training day, because that day's
inhibition cuts the yield of the accumulated signal, and stays below it on
most days of the five-sessions-per-week block (weeks 10 to 13). That is the
interruption of the rise in performance the paper describes for subject 1.

# Replicate Figure 5: effect of one session, and of repeating it

Figure 5 shows the gain in performance owed to a first 200- or 300-tu
session when nothing follows it, and when the same session is repeated on
the next one or two days. The gain owed to the first session is performance
with all sessions minus performance with the first one removed.

```{r figure5}
gain_first <- function(dose, n_sessions) {
  days <- 0:20
  run <- function(first) {
    W <- c(if (first) dose else 0, rep(dose, n_sessions - 1))
    ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(
      data.frame(time = seq_along(W) - 1, amt = W, evid = 1L, cmt = "signal") |>
        dplyr::filter(amt > 0),
      data.frame(time = days, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "perf")
    ) |>
      dplyr::mutate(id = 1L) |>
      dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))
    out <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, returnType = "data.frame")
    out <- out[!duplicated(out$time), ]
    out$perf[match(days, out$time)]
  }
  data.frame(day = days, gain = run(TRUE) - run(FALSE), dose = dose,
             scenario = c("Single session", "Same session next day",
                          "Same session 2 next days")[n_sessions])
}
fig5 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c(200, 300), function(d) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(1:3, function(k) gain_first(d, k)))
}))
fig5$scenario <- factor(fig5$scenario, levels = c("Single session", "Same session next day", "Same session 2 next days"))
ggplot(fig5[fig5$day <= 19, ], aes(day, gain, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ paste0("Effect of a ", dose, "-tu session")) +
  labs(x = "Time after session (days)", y = "Gain in performance (W)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Replicates Figure 5 of Busso 2017")
```

```{r figure5-table}
fig5_peak <- fig5 |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose, scenario) |>
  dplyr::summarise(peak = max(gain), day_of_peak = day[which.max(gain)], day19 = gain[day == 19],
                   .groups = "drop")
# Figure 5 read by the maintainers (axis 0-7 W): peak gain and gain at day 19.
fig5_paper <- data.frame(
  dose = rep(c(200, 300), each = 3),
  scenario = levels(fig5$scenario)[c(1:3, 1:3)],
  peak_fig = c(4.07, 3.72, 3.42, 5.75, 4.93, 4.33),
  day19_fig = c(3.33, 3.05, 2.85, 4.73, 4.12, 3.65)
)
fig5_cmp <- dplyr::left_join(fig5_peak, fig5_paper, by = c("dose", "scenario"))
fig5_cmp |>
  dplyr::transmute(Dose = dose, Scenario = scenario,
                   "Peak (sim)" = round(peak, 2), "Peak (Figure 5)" = peak_fig,
                   "Day of peak (sim)" = day_of_peak,
                   "Day 19 (sim)" = round(day19, 2), "Day 19 (Figure 5)" = day19_fig) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Figure 5 against the packaged model with the median estimates.")
# Deterministic simulation against values read off the published figure; the
# read-off is good to about 0.05-0.1 W.
stopifnot(
  max(abs(fig5_cmp$peak / fig5_cmp$peak_fig - 1)) < 0.05,
  max(abs(fig5_cmp$day19 / fig5_cmp$day19_fig - 1)) < 0.05,
  all(fig5_cmp$day_of_peak %in% 8:11)
)
```

The simulated curves sit 1% to 3% under the values read off the figure,
uniformly across the six curves. The one-day gain (0.87 W for 200 tu,
0.85 W for 300 tu) and the ranking of the scenarios agree.

# Replicate Figure 6: steady state and the optimal daily dose

When the same dose is repeated every day the system reaches a steady state.
Equating successive days of the recursion gives

`Perf_ss = Perf0 + kon_s (1 - kin_i W) W / ((1 - exp(-koff)) (1 - exp(-(kout_s + kon_s (1 - kin_i W)))))`,

an inverted U in the daily dose `W`. The packaged ODE is simulated for
600 days of daily training (18 half-lives of `koff`) and compared with that
closed form.

```{r figure6}
perf_ss <- function(W, perf0, koff, kon_s, kout_s, kin_i) {
  inhib <- kin_i * W
  perf0 + kon_s * (1 - inhib) * W /
    ((1 - exp(-koff)) * (1 - exp(-(kout_s + kon_s * (1 - inhib)))))
}
doses <- seq(0, 490, by = 10)
ev6 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(doses), function(k) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    if (doses[k] > 0) data.frame(time = 0:599, amt = doses[k], evid = 1L, cmt = "signal"),
    data.frame(time = 600, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "perf")
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(id = k)
})) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
# Tight tolerances: at the default rtol = 1e-6 the integration error builds
# up over 600 dosing intervals to a few hundredths of a W.
sim6 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev6, returnType = "data.frame",
                        rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-10, maxsteps = 1e6)
fig6 <- data.frame(W = doses, perf = sim6$perf[match(seq_along(doses), sim6$id)])
fig6$closed_form <- perf_ss(fig6$W, 250, meds[["koff"]], meds[["kon_s"]], meds[["kout_s"]], meds[["kin_i"]])
max(abs(fig6$perf - fig6$closed_form))
# Same parameters on both sides: after 600 days exp(-koff * 600) ~ 1e-8 of
# the start-up transient is left, so the gap is integration error only.
stopifnot(max(abs(fig6$perf - fig6$closed_form)) < 0.005)
ggplot(fig6, aes(W, perf)) +
  geom_line() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(200, 400)) +
  labs(x = "Daily training dose (tu)", y = "Performance at steady state (W)",
       title = "Replicates Figure 6 of Busso 2017")
```

```{r figure6-optimum}
opt <- optimize(function(W) -perf_ss(W, 250, meds[["koff"]], meds[["kon_s"]], meds[["kout_s"]], meds[["kin_i"]]),
                c(0, 490))
c(optimal_dose_tu = opt$minimum, peak_W = -opt$objective,
  perf_at_490_tu = fig6$perf[fig6$W == 490])
# Figure 6 (read by the maintainers): peak about 366 W near 245 tu; about
# 245 W at 490 tu.
stopifnot(
  abs(-opt$objective - 366) < 3,
  abs(opt$minimum - 245) < 15,
  abs(fig6$perf[fig6$W == 490] - 245) < 5
)
```

The Discussion gives the optimal daily dose from Model TI as 253 +/- 45 tu
(mean +/- SD over the six subjects). With each subject's Table 2 estimates:

```{r optimum-by-subject}
opt_subj <- vapply(1:6, function(j) {
  p <- tab2[j, ]
  optimize(function(W) -perf_ss(W, 250, p$koff, p$kon_s, p$kout_s, p$kin_i), c(0, 600))$minimum
}, numeric(1))
round(opt_subj, 1)
c(mean = mean(opt_subj), sd = sd(opt_subj))
stopifnot(abs(mean(opt_subj) - 253) < 2, abs(sd(opt_subj) - 45) < 2)
```

The optimum does not depend on `Perf0`, which only shifts the curve.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Daily recursion, not the printed ODEs.** The paper's estimates belong to
  the discrete recursion of Equations 7 to 14, which the authors fitted and
  simulated with. The packaged ODE reproduces that recursion exactly at whole
  days (Check 1) by adjusting the production coefficient within each day.
  Solving Equations 1 to 4 literally would change the gain from a session by
  about 16% for the median parameters. Between whole days performance is a
  smooth interpolation the paper does not define.
* **Order of the inhibition term in the signal decay.** Equation 13 prints
  `Signal(i) = Signal(i-1) exp(-kout_s - kon_s (1 - Inhib(i))) + W(i)`, with
  the same day's inhibition. The authors' spreadsheet (sheet `Model_TI`,
  column E) uses `Inhib(i - 1)`, the previous day's, and reproduces the
  published fit of subject 1 to the last digit (RSS 1393.03, adj. R2 0.96699).
  The model follows the spreadsheet. The production term (Equation 14) uses
  the same day's inhibition in both.
* **Equation 2** prints `Prec` in place of `Signal`.
* **Table 1, subject 1, Model TI AICc** is printed as 291.07. The authors'
  spreadsheet computes 291.17 from the same fit, as does this vignette; the
  spreadsheet's Model T value (328.04) matches Table 1 exactly.
* **Typical values** are the medians of the six Table 2 estimates (0.03055,
  0.00739, 0.2915, 0.00206). The Results text prints them rounded (0.0305,
  0.0074, 0.292, 0.0021). Figure 6 is reproduced with the unrounded medians
  (peak 366.6 W at 244 tu, 245.5 W at 490 tu) and not with the rounded ones
  (364.6 W at 239 tu, 236.2 W at 490 tu), so the unrounded medians are what
  the paper simulated with.
* **Baseline.** `Perf0` is fixed at 250 W (Figure 6). In the fits each
  subject's `Perf0` was their first measured performance, and it should be
  set the same way when simulating an individual.
* **No between-subject variability.** Each subject was fitted separately and
  no population variance was estimated, so the model has no `eta` terms. The
  spread of the individual estimates is in Table 2 (large for `kon_s` and
  `kout_s` because of subject 6).
* **Residual error** is not printed in the paper. The likelihood (Equation 18)
  profiles the residual variance out, so each subject's maximum-likelihood
  `sigma` is `sqrt(RSS / n)`. The packaged 6.02 W is the median over the six
  subjects of that value, computed by the maintainers above.
* **Figure 5** is reproduced 1% to 3% below the values read off the figure,
  uniformly across scenarios; the read-off itself is uncertain by about
  0.05 to 0.1 W.
* **Event records.** Training is entered as one bolus into `signal` per day,
  at the start of the day, with the day's training units as the amount. The
  inhibition reads that dose for one day (`tad(signal) < 1`), so two
  training records on one day, or a record that is not at the start of the
  day, break the daily semantics of the model.
* **No NCA.** The endpoint is a physiological performance measure, not a drug
  concentration, so the PKNCA section of a popPK validation does not apply;
  the recursion, goodness-of-fit and steady-state checks above take its
  place.
